hook: The LOX at *30*: Still Here, Still Undefeated
dek: From Yonkers to Verzuz, how Jadakiss, Styles P and Sheek Louch never broke up.

slides.label: Yonkers Roots
slides.text: Jadakiss and Sheek's grandmothers lived next door in Yonkers. A demo through *Mary J. Blige* landed them at Bad Boy in 1996.

slides.label: 24 Hrs. to Live
slides.text: Before their own album, they stole the show on *24 Hrs. to Live* with Mase, Black Rob and DMX. Then came platinum debut *Money, Power & Respect* in 1998.

slides.label: Reservoir Dogs
slides.text: On Jay-Z's *'Reservoir Dogs'* in 1998, Bad Boy, Roc-A-Fella and Yonkers shared one track, and nobody took a verse off.

slides.label: Let The LOX Go
slides.text: Feeling watered down at Bad Boy, they launched *'Let The LOX Go'* and left for Ruff Ryders, where *We Are the Streets* hit No. 5 in 2000.

slides.label: Solo, Still Together
slides.text: Jadakiss, Styles P and Sheek Louch each hit the *Top 10* solo, built D-Block, and kept coming back as The LOX anyway.

slides.label: Verzuz Night
slides.text: Aug. 3, 2021: The LOX ran through Dipset at Madison Square Garden. Jadakiss's freestyle over *'Who Shot Ya?'* broke the internet.

slides.label: Still Here
slides.text: 2026: a Tribeca documentary, Styles P's final album, and Rock The Bells on Nov. 29. *'Loyalty is royalty.'*

question: Who's your favorite LOX member, and has it changed?
first_comment: Our founder's answer: Sheek Louch first, then Styles P, then Jadakiss. Who's yours?

caption_instagram:
The Lox at 30 means three friends from Yonkers who never broke up, even when the solo money came. Jadakiss, Styles P and Sheek Louch started as teenagers rapping as the Bomb Squad, got signed to Bad Boy through a demo that reached Mary J. Blige, and left for Ruff Ryders when they felt watered down.

They ran through Dipset on Verzuz, dropped three Top 10 solo albums without ever splitting, and still show up as The LOX, over and over, for three decades.

This year brought a Tribeca documentary, Styles P's final album and a Nov. 29 date at Rock The Bells in Newark with LL COOL J, SWV, Method Man & Redman and Lil' Kim.

Who's your favorite LOX member, and has it changed over the years?

caption_linkedin:
The Lox at 30 is a case study in brand discipline most founders never learn. Three teenagers from Yonkers signed to Bad Boy in 1996, realized the label's image did not fit who they were, and walked away from it publicly with a 'Let The LOX Go' campaign rather than keep cashing checks on someone else's terms.

They rebuilt at Ruff Ryders, then did something rare: each member built a separate Top 10 solo career, started their own label, D-Block, and still kept coming back together instead of letting the solo wins split the group.

Three decades later: a Tribeca documentary, a farewell solo album from Styles P, and a festival headline slot, all without ever losing the original three.

Knowing when to walk away from a deal that does not fit, and then building your own lane instead, might be the most underrated founder move in this story.

Who is your favorite LOX member, and has it changed over the years?
